"When he came over, all he ate was meat, eggs, raw milk and things like that. It’s on his YouTube channel now I think.

"He was very on it with his stuff and he just eats very, very simply every night. I’m pretty sure he barbecues every night as well, from what I’ve been told."

Haaland's diet has helped him score a staggering 159 goals in 194 appearances for City since joining the club in 2022.



The forward has also found the net 55 times in just 49 caps for Norway.

Sports.title: Manchester United target West Ham star in surprise transfer raid
Sports.content:
Manchester United are interested in West Ham United's El Hadji Malick Diouf, talkSPORT understands.

The 21-year-old Hammers star has been a standout player for West Ham in a difficult season.

3 Diouf has been a key part of the West Ham team Credit: AFP

Despite the Hammers battling relegation all year, Diouf has impressed at left-back.



The Senegal international has been marauding up and down the left for the Irons and earned plaudits following his move from Sparta Prague in 2025.

West Ham spent £22million plus add-ons for Diouf.

But he has made 28 Premier League appearances and has five assists, and it would have been more if it weren't for the Africa Cup of Nations.

Diouf played five games as Senegal beat Morocco in one of the most controversial finals of recent times.

He played all 120 minutes of the final and lifted the trophy that has since been awarded to Morocco.



There is no indication of what sort of fee West Ham would be looking for but a lot would depend on the relegation battle.

Nuno Espirito Santo's side are two points clear of Tottenham in 17th place with four games to go.



So, fees for any players leaving the London Stadium likely will depend on if the Irons go down or stay up.

Man United's transfer strategy

In terms of left-back, manager Michael Carrick has entrusted Luke Shaw with his place.



Patrick Dorgu is also an option, but the Denmark international has been injured for a few months, and even when he was playing, he was deployed further forward.

Shaw isn't getting any younger and Dorgu is more of a wing-back, which explains why Diouf would be a target.

3 Should Carrick stay or go, a new left-back is on the cards at Old Trafford Credit: Getty

The Red Devils also aren't shying away from their need to improve the centre of midfield.

Casemiro has been announced to be leaving while talkSPORT understands that the club are willing to listen to offers for Manuel Ugarte.



After joining for £50million in the summer of 2024 from Paris Saint-Germain to become the first INEOS signing, the club are willing to accept an offer at half of that price.

Kobbie Mainoo has signed a new deal that will see him earn around £150,000 per week and keep him at Old Trafford until 2031.

But away from that, Atalanta's Ederson has emerged as a target.

talkSPORT understands the Italian side value the Brazilian at £42million.

He has agreed terms with Atletico Madrid, but the Champions League semi-finalists are yet to sort terms with Atalanta.

Sandro Tonali, Carlos Baleba, Elliot Anderson and Adam Wharton are also on the radar.



3 Mainoo will be the only central midfielder to remain with a big revamp on the way Credit: AFP

One position that isn't a concern for Man United is centre-back with Carrick adamant they won't be looking for more central defenders.

He said: “It’s not an area of concern for me at this moment in time.

“At the moment and timing wise, talking about the summer and what goes beyond that, it’s difficult to elaborate on that really.

“Licha’s [Lisandro Martinez] missing games for different reasons at the minute, which we won’t go into, but I understand why you are asking it.

“But no, I haven’t got concerns. I think we’ve got a mixed blend there of experience, of real quality and some young – I’d say more than talented really – two promising young players that have already shown what they can do.



“I thought Ayden was fantastic last week in such a difficult game.

“I haven’t got concerns. What the future looks like, I can’t really get involved, because I’m not sure myself what that looks like.”

Sports.title: Eddie Howe in face-to-face talks with the man who just binned off LIV Golf
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe in face-to-face talks with the man who just binned off LIV Golf

Eddie Howe is set for face-to-face talks with Newcastle chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan at the annual PIF summit.

The summit comes just hours after the latter pulled funding for LIV Golf.

3 Howe will be asked to explain just why the Premier League form has declined so badly Credit: Getty

As the Toon's majority owners, the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund meet with the day-to-day runners of the club every year to discuss strategy, the season and transfer plans.

talkSPORT understands these talks were scheduled to happen at this time at the start of the season but they of course come amid a backdrop of a terrible domestic campaign for the Toon.

Newcastle have lost nine of their last 12 in the Premier League and face being dragged into a late relegation battle with their form a major cause for concern for their fans.

Al-Rumayyan and several other PIF officials will meet Howe, CEO David Hopkinson and sporting director Ross Wilson.

They are set for two days of talks at Maften Hall just north of Newcastle, and there are plenty of things to discuss.

Howe's future is up in the air, with talkSPORT understanding that the Englishman could walk away from St James' Park at the end of the season.

His time on Tyneside has been extremely successful, qualifying for the Champions League twice and claiming the Carabao Cup - for which he will always be celebrated as it ended the club's 70-year wait without a trophy.

However, with four games to go, Newcastle are on course for a lower bottom half finish and have thrown away 25 points from winning positions this term to leave some Toon fans feeling as if a change in the dugout would be best.

At this summit, Howe will be given the opportunity to explain where he believes things have gone wrong.

Hopkinson also revealed that Newcastle's transfer strategy would be changing, and the final item on the agenda is a potential new training ground and a plan for St James' Park.

The club are yet to decide if they want to expand the current ground or build a new stadium, and it is something that has been discussed for years.

Hopkinson also revealed on talkSPORT earlier this year that by 2030, he wants the Magpies to be regularly competing for the top trophies in the world.

So, it's unclear how the ownership will judge this year for the Magpies in relation to that target.

3 Al-Rumayyan doesn't really have a hands-on-role with Newcastle, but he'll wants answers Credit: Getty

LIV Golf gone

The summit comes amid, PIF have pulling their funding from LIV Golf, which was Al-Rumayyan's breakaway league from the traditional PGA Tour.

The PIF have ploughed billions into it, but the funding has been cut.

In a statement, they said: "PIF has made the decision to fund LIV Golf only for the remainder of the 2026 season.

"The substantial investment required by LIV Golf over a longer term is no longer consistent with the current phase of PIF's investment strategy. This decision has been made in light of PIF's investment priorities and current macro dynamics."

For Newcastle fans concerned, there are numerous reports that suggest nothing is changing for their club.

However, there is a clear reduction in investment in sports from the Saudis, and we should know where things stand with Newcastle soon.

3 Howe has looked increasingly perplexed on the sidelines Credit: Getty

talkSPORT verdict - golf correspondent Sean O'Brien Yasir Al-Rumayyan is the man who runs the Public Investment Fund and essentially controls the Saudi billions. LIV Golf was his passion project. Rory McIlroy and many others have been on record crediting Al-Rumayyan with a genuine love for the game. At times, his enthusiasm for LIV Golf felt like the only other thing keeping it alive besides the money. By pulling the plug completely, Al-Rumayyan has all-but accepted that he lost billions and failed in his objectives. And just hours after that news was made public, Eddie Howe has to meet him in person and explain why Newcastle are so crap right now. While this is said to be a long-planned annual debrief, rather than showdown talks, the timing is fascinating.

Hopkinson's blueprint

Ahead of the PIF summit, Hopkinson was in London and set out a clear plan to grow Newcastle's revenue.

He said: "Our ambition is ultimately to be number one. How are we going to do that? Frankly, money is the biggest piece of the equation.

“We’ve got to just generate more revenue, give ourselves a bigger envelope to work with. If we can execute superbly, there might be £100m in annual run rate revenue that could be unlocked.

"We’re [at] about £400m. Well, that can become £500m or stretch to £550m. We start to kick our way into that conversation. That’s our ambition.

“We don’t have an insurance sponsor today - we should have one. The training ground didn’t have naming rights - it does now.

“Stadium naming rights, expanding our digital audience, all of that can unlock revenue. If we execute superbly, there might be £100m in annual run-rate revenue that could be unlocked.”

With that in mind, Newcastle are set to appoint Dave O'Connor as chief revenue officer and a new chief marketing officer is set to be brought in as well.

Sports.title: Michael Yormark blown away by ‘incredible’ $1bn Messi stadium in Miami as Vinicius eyes ‘very active’ World Cup
Sports.content:
Michael Yormark was blown away by seeing Inter Miami's Nu Stadium and Lionel Messi stands in person, and is eagerly anticipating a historic World Cup for Brazil's Vinicius Junior.

Michael Yormark blown away by ‘incredible’ $1bn Messi stadium in Miami as Vinicius eyes ‘very active’ World Cup

Photographs of New York and Los Angeles decorated a wall as the sun poured through a London office.

A sign stating 'Work Hard, Have Fun, Make History' hovered near a desk inside Roc Nation Sports International's headquarters.

6 Michael Yormark is ready for an 'amazing' World Cup that will feature Vinicius Junior Credit: Roc Nation Sports

World Cup countdown is on for USA and Brazil

With the official countdown clock for the 2026 FIFA World Cup down to 42 days, a breakthrough years in the making is almost here for a talent management agency that was founded by rapper and media mogul Jay-Z.

"It goes without saying that this World Cup arguably will be the biggest sporting event in the history of sport," Michael Yormark, president of Roc Nation Sports, exclusively told talkSPORT on Thursday.

"You think about three continents. You think about 48 teams -- international teams. It's the biggest World Cup, right? You think about 104 matches.

"I've heard the (FIFA) president Gianni Infantino say it's 104 Super Bowls. And so when you think about that in that context, it's going to be amazing.

Lionel Messi and his wife appear on infamous Coldplay kiss cam that went viral

"We'll have anywhere between 10 to 16 athletes, clients in the World Cup representing multiple countries. It's a huge moment. It's a huge platform. And it's a huge opportunity for them as it relates to their own brand building."

Vinicius Junior (Real Madrid, Brazil) and Chris Richards (Crystal Palace, USA) highlight the Roc Nation athletes aiming for World Cup glory in an expanded tournament that could create $13 billion in revenue and is expected to take over the United States in June and July.

Yormark said the agency has at least 30 commercial partnerships for players that will be in the World Cup, with brands securing deals to use the athletes' marketing power as an entry point to a tournament that will bounce from Mexico City and Toronto, Canada to Seattle, New York/New Jersey and Dallas in the USA.

Vinicius Junior 'very active' with World Cup promotions

"We've been very, very fortunate," Yormark said.

"When you have high profile players -- obviously we represent quite a few players on Brazil, led by Vinicius Junior. He's been very active. He's got incredible partners for the World Cup

"We've got Chris Richards, who we call Captain America, and Chris has benefited from this moment."

6 Vinicius Junior will go global again during the 2026 World Cup with Brazil Credit: getty

6 Chris Richards has become one of USMNT's best players Credit: getty

Thirty-two years after a USA-hosted World Cup led to the creation of MLS, Yormark witnessed the newest high for American soccer by taking in Inter Miami's state-of-the-art Nu Stadium in person.

While Lionel Messi (Argentina) stands near the top of the Eastern Conference in MLS, one of the biggest names in the international football world now plays his club games inside a 26,700-capacity venue that features a Leo Messi stand and is the $1bn centerpiece of a 131-acre entertainment district.

Messi's new stadium in Miami was 'incredible'

"It is one of the finest stadiums I've ever been in. I mean, incredible," Yormark said.

"I give a lot of credit to the Mas family and David Beckham and everybody involved in that organization. To have the vision that they had and to be able to execute that vision and bring it to life is absolutely incredible.

"I've told people ever since I left that stadium that night, which was this past Saturday, that it is truly one of the best stadiums in the world.

"From a sightline perspective, from the overall footprint of the building -- to all the hospitality areas, to the finishings, to the service levels within the building -- absolutely incredible."

6 Nu Stadium is a breakthrough for American soccer Credit: Getty

6 David Beckham played a role in giving Lionel Messi a new football home Credit: instagram @davidbeckham

6 Messi will defend Argentina's World Cup trophy this summer Credit: Roc Nation Sports/Getty

Yormark's unique sports background has crossed oceans and continents, and gives him rare insight into the global marketing potential of a 2026 World Cup that will mostly be played on American soil.

He started in corporate sponsorship sales with the New York Yankees and spent 12 years with the NHL's Florida Panthers, including serving as the team's president.

Yormark linked to Miami Hurricanes AD gig

Yormark has recently been linked to the Miami Hurricanes athletic director job.

Dan Radakovich will be retiring as Miami AD on June 1.

"Thank you for everything, Dan!" the Hurricanes tweeted.

"From a CFP National Championship appearance to record-breaking GPAs and a 94% graduation rate, he’s leaving The U having made a tremendous impact."

Yormark declined to comment when asked about Miami's AD position.

For Vinicius Junior, Richards and soccer fans from New York to Los Angeles, the 2026 World Cup is almost here.

It will likely take a strong run from Mauricio Pochettino's USMNT squad for the beautiful game to maintain its summer surge in the United States.

"Obviously winning the World Cup would be a dream of mine. And what better time to do it on home soil?" Richards exclusively told talkSPORT in March.

"I can't even begin to describe what it's going to be like. I'm just super excited for the moment."

But the biggest -- and most expensive -- World Cup in history will be must-watch TV across the globe, no matter how far USMNT goes.

Yan Diomande set to represent Ivory Coast

"We've got a lot of players that we want to support," Yormark said.

"Obviously, Vini and all of our players on Team Brazil. We signed Yan Diomande, who's just having a spectacular year at (RB) Leipzig, and he plays in Philadelphia to start the World Cup.

"It's a big moment for our players. But it's also a big moment for Roc Nation Sports International, because when you think about having 10 to 16 players in the World Cup -- based on where we came from and where we started -- it's a great achievement for us, as well."

Stay up to date with the latest from the World Cup across all platforms - follow our dedicated talkSPORT USA Facebook page and subscribe to our talkSPORT USA YouTube channel for all the news, exclusives, interviews and more.

Sports.title: Aston Villa vs Tottenham betting tips and predictions: Can Spurs get back-to-back wins?
Sports.content:
Aston Villa vs Tottenham betting tips and predictions: Can Spurs get back-to-back wins?

Aston Villa and Tottenham clash at Villa Park on Sunday night in the Premier League with the visitors desperate for three points in the bid to avoid relegation.

Aston Villa vs Tottenham best bets

1 Aston Villa vs Tottenham betting tips, predictions, team news, how to watch

Aston Villa vs Tottenham head to head overview
